FASHION E-COMMERCE · 10 MIN

Virtual Try-On Prompts for Fashion E-commerce.

Preserve garment construction while creating believable fit and drape.

Published September 3, 2026Editorial team · PromptStudio AI

A useful virtual try-on image must preserve both the person and the garment. If either changes, the result may be attractive but commercially misleading.

IN THIS GUIDE1. Prepare garment and model references2. Describe construction, not just style3. Direct fit and physical interaction4. Use try-on imagery responsibly

Prepare garment and model references

Use a clean front-facing garment image or ghost-mannequin shot with accurate color. The model reference should show the intended pose, body proportions and unobstructed areas where the garment will sit.

Patterns, trims and closures need enough resolution to survive the transformation. Include additional views for complex backs, sleeves or asymmetric construction.

Describe construction, not just style

List neckline, sleeve length, hem, seams, fasteners, pockets, pattern placement and fabric. Describe fabric weight because silk, denim and wool fold differently.

Tell the model not to redesign the garment or change body proportions. Styling preferences should never override product accuracy.

Direct fit and physical interaction

Specify intended fit—relaxed, tailored, oversized or close-fitting—and ask for natural tension around shoulders, elbows and waist. Hair, hands and accessories should occlude fabric correctly.

Check gravity, mirrored details and repeated patterns. Garments often look plausible until compared directly with the product photo.

Use try-on imagery responsibly

Do not claim exact fit when the image is synthetic. Provide real measurements, size information and conventional product photographs alongside generated imagery.

Use diverse, permissioned model references and avoid changing protected personal characteristics without consent.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
  • Use high-quality garment references.
  • Describe construction and fabric.
  • Protect model and product proportions.
  • Audit pattern and seam placement.
  • Pair synthetic imagery with real product information.
